model.title: CBSE Class 11: ideal projectile experiment
model.description: Bounded analytic projectile motion with synchronized coordinates, first-contact clamping and trial predictions. Unqualified proposal for human review.
assumptions: Illustrative adjustable defaults: angle 45 degrees, speed 10 m/s, launch height 0 m, Earth gravity 9.81 m/s2, target position 10 m, elapsed time 0 s.

Supported inputs: angle 0..1.5707963267948966 radians; speed 1..20 m/s; height 0..10 m; target position 0..520 m; elapsed time 0..30 s. Gravity is a discrete selector allowing only Earth 9.81 or Moon 1.62 m/s2.
Angle display_scale=57.29577951308232 and display_unit=degrees; calculations use dimensionless radians.
Uniform downward gravity, ideal point mass, no drag or spin. Initial position is (0,height); initial velocity is (speed*cos(angle),speed*sin(angle)). Ground is y=0.
Fixed quantities: horizontal launch origin 0 m, ground height 0 m, arithmetic factors 2, 0.5 and 1. Gravity values are approximate teaching values.
time_experiment: time_input=elapsed; step_seconds=0.02; playback_speed=1; reset_on_change=[angle,speed,height,gravity,target]. Parameter changes reset elapsed time atomically.
Time controls must provide launch, pause, resume and reset. Pause freezes the single elapsed-time input; launch starts at zero; stop playback when ground_contact=1. Both coordinates use clamped_time.

The closed-form response integrates constant acceleration from the declared initial conditions. Contact time is the nonnegative quadratic root. A horizontal ground-level launch has zero duration and is immediately stopped.

Use x horizontally and y vertically, in metres, with identical scene scale on both axes. Fit the conservative envelope x=0..520 m and y=0..134 m without independent axis stretching; compared trials share the scale.
Launcher muzzle follows launcher_height at x=0 and its elevation follows launcher_angle. Target reference follows target_x at ground_y. Ball centre follows ball_x and ball_y.
The large visible ball marker is explicitly illustrative; its size does not affect ground contact. Ground, launcher and target remain identifiable and inspectable.
Keep apparatus primary and omit trajectory curves and graphs by default. Any later trajectory must evaluate this law with its identified trial parameters, never a decorative fixed path.
limitations: Excludes launcher acceleration, finite-radius contact, target collision, post-impact motion, air resistance, spin and real-world performance validation.
Scalar equations provide positions, predictions and stop signals, not a playback state machine. The interaction layer must enforce the specified atomic reset, pause and first-contact stop behavior.
Use the existing exact model snapshot and reference readouts for trial comparison, including gravity. This proposal does not implement an arbitrary multi-trial archive.
Optional retained paths would require sampling each saved trial's equations and consistent scales; no path storage or graph implementation is claimed here.

All outputs are bounded: duration and clamped time 0..26 s; landing distance and ball x 0..520 m; peak and ball y 0..134 m; time remaining 0..26 s; flags 0 or 1; launcher angle 0..pi/2; launcher height 0..10 m; target x 0..520 m; ground y 0 m.

snapshot.unfinished_question: How do launch angle, speed and gravity change a ball's flight? Build a CBSE Class 11 projectile-motion experiment with a clearly visible launcher, a moving ball, ground and a target. Let me change angle, speed, launch height and Earth or Moon gravity, launch and pause the flight, inspect parts, and compare trials. The ball must move in both horizontal and vertical directions from the calculated position, stopping at first ground contact. Show flight duration, landing distance and peak height. Use a compact schematic scene with one consistent coordinate scale and a large visible ball marker; explain that marker size is illustrative. The target and launcher must follow their settings. Keep the apparatus primary and graphs optional. Do not display a fixed trajectory as though it updates with settings.

limits: Positions use 0.1 scene unit per metre equally on all axes; equations retain SI units. Apparatus and marker dimensions are schematic.
Exactly four visible parts; no decorative trajectory or graphs.

Ideal point mass under uniform downward gravity; excludes air resistance, spin, launcher acceleration, finite-radius contact, target collision and post-impact motion. No real-world validation is claimed.
Ball marker diameter is 0.12 scene unit and is illustrative. First ground contact occurs when its centre reaches y=0, regardless of marker size.
Preserve accepted inputs, defaults, equations and IDs: angle 0..pi/2 radians, speed 1..20 m/s, height 0..10 m, target 0..520 m, elapsed 0..30 s; named gravity choices Earth 9.81 and Moon 1.62 m/s².
Launcher rotates about its muzzle and moves vertically with launch height. Target moves horizontally only, with its base at ground level.
Subsequent motion must cover verified ball_x 0..548.360580833211 m and ball_y 0..558.360580833211 m at the common 0.1 scale; these conservative verified bounds are not simultaneous physical extrema.

Both ball coordinates use one clamped clock; launch, pause, resume and reset remain synchronized. Playback end_time_id is duration; zero-duration launches stop immediately. Settings changes reset atomically, including target changes; runtime frames the complete finite path automatically without unequal axis scaling; all translations remain within ±100 scene units at the declared scale, and default

parts.label: Launcher
parts.explanation: The launcher points in the launch direction. Its muzzle, the opening where the ball starts, follows the selected height.

parts.label: Ball marker
parts.explanation: This marker shows the calculated ball position. Its size is illustrative; ground contact is measured at its centre.

parts.label: Level ground
parts.explanation: The ground marks zero height. The flight ends when the ball's centre reaches this level.

parts.label: Ground target
parts.explanation: The target slides along the ground to mark an aiming distance. It does not cause a collision in this model.

experiments.title: Earth versus Moon
experiments.prompt: Keep angle, speed and height fixed. Predict how Moon gravity changes flight duration, then compare snapshots.
experiments.explanation: Lower gravity increases flight duration for a nonzero-duration launch. Compare landing distance and peak height too; snapshots retain gravity.

experiments.title: Change launch angle
experiments.prompt: At the default speed, ground-level height and Earth gravity, predict how changing 45 degrees to 30 degrees affects landing distance.
experiments.explanation: At equal launch and landing heights, range depends on both horizontal velocity and flight duration. Hold all other settings fixed.

experiments.title: Increase initial speed
experiments.prompt: Keep angle, height and gravity fixed. Predict how increasing speed from 10 to 15 m/s changes peak height.
experiments.explanation: Peak height equals launch height plus the squared initial vertical velocity divided by twice gravity.

experiments.title: Raise the launcher
experiments.prompt: Keep angle, speed and gravity fixed. Predict how raising the muzzle from 0 to 5 m changes flight duration.
experiments.explanation: A higher launch point increases time to ground contact. The launcher muzzle follows height; the target stays at ground level.

controls.help: Changes launcher elevation and both initial velocity components; changing it restarts time.
Changes initial velocity magnitude and flight predictions; changing it restarts time.
Raises the launcher muzzle and initial ball position, changing contact time and peak height.
Selects approximate Earth or Moon gravity, changing downward acceleration and restarting time.
Moves the ground-level aiming reference horizontally and resets time; it does not change flight or cause collisions.
Advances both calculated coordinates together, clamped at first contact; pause freezes both coordinates.

time_experiment.explanation: Launch starts at zero; pause freezes the shared clock, resume continues it, and reset returns it to zero. Settings changes restart time atomically. From initial position (0,height), velocity (speed*cos(angle),speed*sin(angle)) and constant downward gravity, both coordinates use time clamped to duration. Playback stops at duration, immediately for zero-duration launches. The illustrative 0.12-scene-unit marker contacts ground at its centre, not its surface.

coverage.explanation: Compare exact model snapshots with other settings fixed. The same launch parameters determine all three predictions under uniform gravity without drag or spin.
Launch parameters determine contact duration and landing position. Both ball coordinates share the clamped clock; launch, pause, resume and reset preserve synchronization and stop at first contact.
Angle and height drive launcher pose and flight predictions. Inspect all four parts. The separate target control moves only its ground-level reference horizontally, without affecting flight.
Compare snapshot predictions using the common 0.1-scene-unit-per-metre scale on both axes. Marker size is illustrative; contact uses its centre. An arbitrary multi-trial archive is not implemented.
Inspect the apparatus-first schematic. Graphs and trajectories are omitted; any future path must be calculated from and identified with its trial settings.

outcomes: Investigate angle, initial speed, launch height and Earth/Moon gravity by comparing flight duration, landing distance and peak height.
Launch and pause a ball whose horizontal and vertical positions are calculated together, stopping at first ground contact.
Inspect a visible launcher, ball, ground and horizontally adjustable ground-level target; apparatus positions must follow their controls.
Compare trials in a compact schematic using equal horizontal and vertical coordinate scales and a large, explicitly illustrative ball marker.
Keep the apparatus primary and graphs optional; any displayed trajectory must correspond to its identified trial settings.

generation_quality.scope: Recipe, label, connection and dependency checks only. Dependency paths do not prove numeric change. Overlap, recognizability, physical correctness and child usability require separate evaluation.

visual.scope: Eight fitted views; projected bounds, center-ray occlusion, conservative bounding-box overlaps and estimated two-line label capacity. These heuristics do not replace rendered-image or child usability review.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.

repair_actions.rule: Retries require the existing explicit retry flow. Never edit accepted artifact hashes or automatically spend provider requests.

scene_revision.feedback: Preserve the accepted equations, inputs, defaults, IDs and 0.1 scene-unit/metre positional scale. Fix a specific incompatible construction plan: launcher is an UNATTACHED FREE BODY that rotates about Z AND translates along Y as height changes, so construction_plan launcher.motion_axis MUST BE null and attachment MUST BE null. A z-only motion_axis wrongly forbids height motion. Do not repair this by deleting the height binding. Set launcher base position=(0,0,0), base rotation=(0,0,0). Its two bindings must be rotate Z launcher_angle [0,pi/2] -> [0,90 degrees], and translate Y launcher_height [0,10] -> [0,1]. Use compact launcher length .30 along negative local X ending at muzzle origin, diameter .06. Keep the recent compact scene: ball sphere diameter .12 centered at the bound point (not oversized 1.1); thin ground width56,height.01,depth.10 centered world(27,-.005,0); target width.05,height.24,depth.04 with base at bound ground point. Ball has null motion_axis, independent X and Y translation bindings using exact verified full ranges and .1 scaling; no angular motion. Target moves only X with origin-offset compensation. Ground no motion. Near-front camera along +Z. Do not change positional scale or add a fake static trail. The runtime frames the complete finite path automatically. Learning must keep end_time_id=duration, atomic reset on settings, Earth/Moon named choices and valid guided comparisons. Clearly state schematic point-mass marker size and ground contact at its centre.
